clue.text: Gracious girl coming out and being broadcast

parts.note: a debutante, or deb, is a young woman making her coming-out into society
a programme being broadcast is on air

explanation.surface: A well-mannered young woman makes her society debut while the cameras roll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Coming out' looks like it could signal an anagram or a deletion, but it belongs to the debutante.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: someone suave and courteous in manner is described as gracious.

clue.text: Convey old Bob's demise

parts.note: a bob was the old British slang name for a shilling, abbreviated s
a demise is an end

explanation.surface: A message announcing that an old man called Bob has died.
explanation.walkthrough: Bob is not a man: a 'bob' was a shilling in British pre-decimal money, written s.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to convey a message or parcel is to dispatch it to someone.

clue.text: Father takes advantage of breaks

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father
to take advantage of something is to use it

explanation.surface: Dad exploits the holidays he is given.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: short breaks or rests in activity are halts, plural noun.

clue.text: Computer giant hosting an American gets general approbation

indicators.note: a host holds its guests within, so the first piece goes round the others

parts.note: Apple is the large computer company

explanation.surface: A big technology firm takes on a US employee and wins universal praise.
explanation.definitionFit: Clapping is the public expression of widespread approval.

clue.text: Irritable, having no more classes

definitions.meaning: read literally, having run ..., that is, kinds or categories

explanation.surface: A tetchy student whose timetable has finished for the day.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom for grumpy; read literally, sorts are classes, so lacking them is being without any.

clue.text: Frenchmen, capturing a wild beast, showing bottle

indicators.note: the Frenchmen hold the other letters captive between them

parts.note: MM is the abbreviation for messieurs, French for gentlemen
a gnu, or wildebeest, is the classic crossword wild beast

explanation.surface: French hunters catch a wild animal and show courage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottle' looks like British slang for courage, which suits the surface, but here it is a container.
explanation.definitionFit: A champagne container holding twice the standard 75cl amount is called by this name.

clue.text: Bishop always has time for a drink

parts.note: B is the chess abbreviation for bishop
ever means always, as in 'ever hopeful'
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: A clergyman who never misses his tipple.
explanation.definitionFit: General term: any liquid for drinking, from tea to wine, is one of these.

clue.text: Animation features design of green and yellow, initially

indicators.note: a design arranges something, so the letters of green are rearranged
initially picks the first letter of yellow

explanation.surface: A cartoon whose artwork is coloured green and yellow.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: liveliness or vigour, as in 'she spoke with great animation'.

clue.text: More than one comrade touring Lima, an old city

indicators.note: a comrade going round places surrounds them, so these letters sit inside

parts.note: a pal is a friend or comrade
L is Lima in the NATO phonetic alphabet
Ur is the ancient Mesopotamian city

explanation.surface: Several friends on a trip visiting Lima and an ancient city.
explanation.definitionFit: Grammar term: a form denoting more than a single thing, like 'cats'.

clue.text: Courageous chap embracing sovereign

indicators.note: the chap wraps his arms around the other letter, so it goes inside

parts.note: bod is British slang for a person or chap
a sovereign was a gold pound coin, and L is the abbreviation for pound

explanation.surface: A brave man hugging the monarch.
explanation.walkthrough: The sovereign is not a king but a British gold coin worth a pound, written L (from libra).
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: daring and fearless, as in a brave move.

clue.text: Time for skip to be transported

parts.note: a spell is a period of time
to bound is to leap or skip

explanation.surface: An instruction for when to jump in order to be carried off somewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Transported' suggests travel, but here it means enraptured.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: enraptured or entranced, as when someone is carried away by music.

clue.text: Worries about second stroke

parts.note: cares are worries

explanation.surface: Anxiety over suffering a second stroke.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stroke' suggests a medical event, but here it is a gentle touch.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a tender stroking touch with the hand.

clue.text: Former site of a trade fair

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife
a site is a position or location

explanation.surface: A spot where a commercial show was once held.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a large public exhibition or show of goods, like the Great Exhibition.

clue.text: Leave note without regrets? That's horrible!

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the leave and note go round the regrets

parts.note: to go is to leave
to rue is to regret
me (mi) is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Someone leaving a message without apology, and the response is outrage.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: grisly or ghastly, causing horror.

clue.text: Patrol leader engulfed by storms in cataract

indicators.note: the letter is swallowed up inside the storms

parts.note: to storm a place is to raid it

indicators.note: the leader of the word Patrol is its first letter

explanation.surface: The head of a patrol is overwhelmed by tempests at a waterfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cataract' suggests an eye condition, but here it is a waterfall.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a cataract is a large waterfall or stretch of fast, turbulent river water.

clue.text: Pam ceded building and made off

indicators.note: building constructs something new from the letters, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Pam gave up a building and fled.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to have left suddenly or fled is to have absconded.

clue.text: Shortage of spun thread

indicators.note: spinning twists the letters of thread into a new order

explanation.surface: Not enough thread has been produced on the wheel.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a scarcity or lack of something.

clue.text: Man gets bounty for old insurgent

parts.note: he stands for a man
a bounty is a reward

explanation.surface: A man collects the price on an old rebel's head.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereward the Wake led English resistance to the Norman conquest in the Fens in the 1070s.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: an eleventh-century English rebel leader against William the Conqueror.

clue.text: One checking a canopy

definitions.meaning: someone who checks or tries things out
a canopy over a bed or pulpit

explanation.surface: An inspector of awnings.
explanation.definitionFit: One who tries things out, and also an old word for the canopy over a four-poster bed.

clue.text: Wipe out an extensive area

parts.note: mass means large-scale, as in mass production
an acre is a unit of area

explanation.surface: Clearing a large region of land.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to slaughter wholesale, killing many people.

clue.text: Teresa treated sharp edges

indicators.note: treating something processes and changes it, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Teresa had her cuts dressed after a fall.
explanation.definitionFit: Geology term: knife-edged mountain ridges between glacial valleys.

clue.text: Writer entertains holy man in cafe

indicators.note: a host entertains guests indoors, so the holy man goes inside the writer

parts.note: a biro is a ballpoint pen, something that writes
ST is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: An author treats a priest to a meal in a coffee shop.
explanation.walkthrough: The writer is not an author but a pen: Biro is the British name for a ballpoint.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a small informal restaurant or eatery.

clue.text: Inspiration from touching in jacuzzi

indicators.note: the word touching is put in the jacuzzi

parts.note: a jacuzzi is a type of bath
re means concerning or touching on

explanation.surface: Getting a creative idea from physical contact in a hot tub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Inspiration' suggests a creative spark, but here it means drawing in air.
explanation.definitionFit: Physiology sense: inspiration is inhaling, taking air into the lungs.

clue.text: Length of time in the middle

indicators.note: time is placed in the middle

parts.note: the centre is the middle
taken as written

explanation.surface: A long period at the halfway point of something.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a metric unit of linear measurement, one hundredth of a metre.

clue.text: Enthusiast protects weak young animal

indicators.note: the enthusiast shields the other letter by surrounding it

parts.note: a fan is an enthusiast

explanation.surface: An animal lover shelters a feeble baby creature.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a young deer in its first year.

clue.text: Tense when in charge for function

indicators.note: the tense letter is placed in the charge

parts.note: a fee is a charge
T is the grammatical abbreviation for tense

explanation.surface: Nervous about being accused, before some ceremony.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a function is a social event or public gathering, like a garden party or fair.

clue.text: Fathom the meaning of last month's poem

parts.note: December is the last month of the year, abbreviated Dec
an ode is a lyric poem

explanation.surface: Trying to understand a poem published a month ago.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Last month' suggests the previous month, but it is the final month of the year.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: to decipher or interpret a coded or obscure message.

clue.text: Going round to corrupt a politician

parts.note: to rot is to decay or corrupt
a Tory is a member of the UK Conservative Party

explanation.surface: Doing the rounds trying to bribe a Conservative MP.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: revolving or turning about an axis.
